description:
On macOS, `chief reap` cannot see the one shape of orphan its third key exists to catch — a descendant that has left the run's worktree AND carries an argv with no marker — because the third key reads process environments, and macOS will not show them. The shape is not hypothetical: it was found in the field, burning two cores.

FIELD RECORD, 2026-09-11, macOS 26.5. Four runs across two downstream repositories were cut off around 00:58. Every driver pid was dead, and each state file still said `running`. A manual sweep then found and killed:

  - `UnrealEditor-Cmd -unattended` on a temporary `engine-version-probe-<uuid>.uproject`, launched by a downstream tasklist's run (the only code that spawns it lived on `chief/160` at the time). PPID 1, process-group leader dead, cwd `/Users/Shared/Epic Games/UE_5.8/Engine/Binaries/Mac`, argv carrying no `--chief-run=` marker, 78 minutes old, 99% CPU rising to 199%, and it IGNORED SIGTERM. That is exactly the residual shape `engine/reap.sh` describes — chdir'd out of the worktree AND wearing an argv that says nothing — on the one platform where the key built for it is dark.
  - a product re-export script run by a second downstream repository's tasklist. Its root's cwd was inside that tasklist's worktree, so key 1 would match the root; its children (`uv`, `pytest` at 2.3 GB) had cwds in $TMPDIR.
  - an agora registry (`node src/main.ts`, cwd `agora/registry`, listening on :8899, 2h13m). Most likely from a downstream tasklist's run; that attribution is UNVERIFIED.

After those were killed, `chief reap -n` reported 'no orphaned chief processes of any kind' and — correctly — that the inherited-$CHIEF_RUN_ID key was inactive on this platform, with cwd + argv carrying the sweep. Be precise about what that does and does not prove: reap was run AFTER the kills, so this is not an observation of reap missing the editor. It is a demonstration BY CONSTRUCTION that none of the three keys can see that process on macOS. US-1 turns the construction into an observed failure.

THIS RESOLVES AN UNVERIFIED IN REAP.SH'S OWN NOTES. They say the leaked integration-test servers 'were the suspected escapees, but their cwd was never recorded ... so whether they beat key 1 is UNVERIFIED', and call key 3 'belt-and-braces, not a proven hole'. On macOS it is a proven hole, and `test/reapenv.sh` SKIPS its end-to-end half on macOS — so the shape has ZERO coverage on the platform this fleet actually runs on.

WHY THE WALK LOSES THEM. `stop_reap_tree` and `chief_scan_descendants` walk PPID edges down from the live driver. A process reparented to launchd has no edge back to anything chief can start a walk from. The tree has to be RECORDED while it is still connected.

PROPOSED MECHANISM — choose, measure, justify in notes. A descendant LEDGER: while a run is live, the driver (or the monitor) periodically snapshots its process tree — pid, ppid, START TIME, argv — into the run's state directory. `chief reap` then treats a still-live pid found in a DEAD run's ledger as a candidate if and only if its start time matches the recorded one. PID reuse is the failure to refuse: a recycled pid with a different start time is never a match. The snapshot cadence bounds what can escape between two snapshots; state the bound. Alternatives worth ruling in or out by measurement rather than argument: process-group ids do NOT tie back on their own (observed the same night: an agent's Bash tool put each command in its own process group — pgid 24417, led by a `zsh -c` under a `claude` pid); session behaviour on macOS is unmeasured.

UNION, NEVER REPLACEMENT, AND NO SCOPE WEAKENED. Keys 1-3 keep working exactly as they do. A registered live run and every descendant stay protected; another repo's runs stay out of scope; unresolved processes are still listed LEFT ALONE; every process is still NAMED BEFORE IT IS SIGNALLED.

RELATED, IN OTHER REPOS: downstream tasklists stop an engine outliving its launcher in the first place, and fix the disk leaks found in the same sweep. A reaper is for what escapes anyway, so both halves are wanted.

userStories.title: The field escape is reproduced on macOS, in a test that fails today
acceptanceCriteria: A hermetic test builds the field shape: a descendant of a registered run that chdirs outside the worktree, execs with an argv carrying no `--chief-run=` marker, ignores SIGTERM, and is reparented to launchd when its parent is SIGKILLed. After the run's driver is gone, the test asserts that `chief reap` names that process and stops it.
On the CURRENT engine, on macOS, that test FAILS. The failing output is recorded in notes. It is not SKIPPED — a skip is how this shape stayed invisible.
Where the platform shows process environments (Linux), key 3 is expected to catch it already. Record which result was observed on which platform rather than inferring either.
userStories.notes: OBSERVED FAILURE, macOS 26.5 (Darwin 25.5.0), `bash test/reap-escaped.sh` -> EXIT=1: "REAPESC FAIL: chief reap did not NAME the escaped orphan (pid 52482, UnrealEditor-Cmd -unattended /var/tmp/engine-version-probe-0f3c.uproject)". The key-by-key probe the test prints first: key 1 (cwd) no · key 2 (argv) no · key 3 (inherited $CHIEF_RUN_ID) no, env read "none" — chief_env_key_mode is empty on this host, so key 3 is inert by construction and the shape has no key at all. POSITIVE CONTROL in the same sweep: a sibling that stayed in the worktree (pid 52481, `sleep 900`) WAS named `[cwd] working in reapesc-escrepo · tl-x` and reaped, so the miss is about the escapee, not about the sweep failing to run. The fixture is the field shape in all four respects and each is asserted, not assumed: cwd outside the canonicalised worktree root, argv with no --chief-run=, `trap "" TERM`, and ppid 1 after its parent is SIGKILLed with the run file still reading state=running. NOT SKIPPED on any platform. Linux NOT OBSERVED this iteration — no docker/Linux host available here (`docker info` failed), so I am recording only what I ran; key 3 is expected to catch it there and the test prints the per-key answer so CI will record that reading when US-2 adds the file to the three gate lists. GATES: bash -n clean over bin/chief + engine/*.sh + install.sh + templates/*.sh + test/*.sh; shellcheck -S error: test/reap-escaped.sh CLEAN (exit 0, standalone shellcheck 0.10.0 — brew install failed on /opt/homebrew permissions). The repo-wide run is NOT clean and was already red before this branch: 3 PRE-EXISTING errors, engine/quality.sh:60 SC1073+SC1072 (a prose comment starting "# shellcheck severity …" parses as a directive under newer shellcheck) and engine/sweep.sh:396,404 SC2066 (for repo in "$current"). That is what main CI has been failing on — GitHub run 33978312283, 2026-09-05, BOTH jobs, byte-identical output to mine under shellcheck 0.11.0. Left alone deliberately: the fix is 3 lines in engine/, which would oblige THIS branch a VERSION bump (test/version-bump.sh) plus a README/ROADMAP sync for a change US-1 has nothing to do with; US-2 edits engine/ and owes that bump anyway, so it clears them; test/smoke.sh PASS, test/ratelimit.sh PASS, test/noworkguard.sh PASS; quality ratchet: allowing.

userStories.title: reap finds it on macOS without reading any process's environment
acceptanceCriteria: The chosen key (the ledger, or a measured alternative the notes justify) makes US-1's test pass on macOS with key 3 inactive.
PID reuse is refused. A ledger entry whose pid is alive but whose start time differs from the recorded one is reported LEFT ALONE and never signalled — shown by a test that plants exactly that entry.
reap's report names the new key as the evidence for each process it finds (for example: recorded in run X's ledger at T, start time matched), next to the existing cwd/argv/env evidence.
Keys 1-3 are unchanged, and `test/teardown.sh`, `test/reapenv.sh` and `test/reapscope.sh` stay green.
The startup sweep a `chief run` already performs benefits without a separate code path. Confirm it, and say so in notes.
GATES: `bash -n` + `shellcheck -S error` clean; behavioural core green; `VERSION` bumped (`test/version-bump.sh`); `ROADMAP.md` names this stem (`test/doc-sync.sh`).
userStories.notes:
KEY 4 = the DESCENDANT LEDGER (engine/ledger.sh): the driver records its own process tree — pid, START TIME, command — into $CHIEF_RUNS/<driver pid>.ledger once per scheduler poll, and a still-live pid in a DEAD run's ledger is a candidate whatever its cwd, argv or environment now say. A RECORD, not a search, which is why it works where every search fails: after the driver dies its descendants are re-parented to launchd and no PPID walk reaches them.

OBSERVED, macOS 26.5 (Darwin 25.5.0), `bash test/reap-escaped.sh` -> REAPESC PASS (exit 0, 5.1s), with the per-key probe printed: key 1 (cwd) no · key 2 (argv) no · key 3 (inherited $CHIEF_RUN_ID) no [env read: none] · KEY 4 (recorded in the run's ledger) YES. The sweep then reported `pid 75348 [ledger] recorded in run reapesc-escrepo-4242-1700000000-75336's tree · start time matched` with the evidence line `a run file in .../runs claims this run, and its driver (pid 75336) is gone`, TERMed it, and hard-killed it after the 1s grace because it ignores TERM as the field process did. So US-1's failure is now a pass with key 3 inert by construction on this host.

PID REUSE IS REFUSED — PART B of the same test plants exactly that entry (a DEAD run's ledger naming a pid that is alive, with a start time it never had) and observed: `pid 75945 PID REUSED · LEFT ALONE · run reapesc-escrepo-4242-1700000002-75942 / recorded as starting Thu_Jan_1_00:00:00_1970; the live pid 75945 started Fri_Sep_11_13:22:34_2026`. The bystander was still alive afterwards and appears in no reap line. Both sides of that comparison go through ONE function (chief_ledger_starttime) — a second reader spelling the token differently would not degrade, it would INVERT.

EVIDENCE IS NAMED: `[ledger]` is in the key legend beside [cwd]/[argv]/[env]/[tree], and a [ledger] finding cites the RECORD rather than a process read — "run X recorded this pid in its own process tree at <time>, and its start time still matches, so it is the same process; that run's driver (pid N) is gone". Keyed off the reason the candidate was added, so a pid the cwd key found is never reported under evidence its tag does not name.

KEYS 1-3 UNCHANGED (no line of chief_pids_cwd_under / chief_pids_tagged / chief_pids_env_marked / the three key-3 gates was touched), and OBSERVED GREEN: test/reapscope.sh PASS, test/reapenv.sh PASS, test/teardown.sh PASS, test/sweep.sh PASS.

THE STARTUP SWEEP BENEFITS WITH NO SEPARATE CODE PATH — CONFIRMED two ways. (1) By construction: chief_ledger_scan has exactly ONE call site, inside chief_find_orphans, and both entry points go through it — the driver's startup `chief_reap_orphans "$WT_ROOT" "$CHIEF_RUN_MARKER_REPO" …` and `chief reap`'s chief_reap_main. The run-id prefix the driver already passes scopes the ledger scan to that repo's runs exactly as it scopes keys 2 and 3. (2) By observation: a real `chief run` (test/smoke.sh, prefix kept) wrote `runs/26123.ledger` mid-run naming both of its driver frames with start times — `26733 Fri_Sep_11_13:26:42_2026 bash …/engine/driver.sh --chief-run=repo-1704832284-1789151201-26123` — and the run completed green, so the recording half runs in the real driver and its startup sweep reads the same file any later `chief reap` does. A run's OWN ledger is excluded by run id (and its tree protected anyway), so a sweep can never reap the run performing it.

THE BOUND, stated rather than argued: the cadence is POLL_SECONDS (default 5s), so a process spawned, orphaned AND abandoned inside one poll interval was never recorded. Union, never replacement — this key can only ADD a candidate.

GATES: bash -n clean over bin/chief + engine/*.sh + install.sh + templates/*.sh + test/*.sh. shellcheck -S error CLEAN repo-wide (0.10.0) — which required fixing the 3 errors that have been red on main and on CI (run 33978312283): engine/quality.sh:60 SC1073+SC1072 (a prose comment beginning "# shellcheck …" parses as a directive) and engine/sweep.sh SC2066 x2 (`for repo in "$current"` cannot word-split; now a plain guard). Behavioural core: test/smoke.sh PASS, test/ratelimit.sh PASS, test/noworkguard.sh PASS. quality ratchet vs main: OK — allowing (single_use_functions 61 -> 63, delta +2, tol 2). VERSION 0.9.22 -> 0.9.23 and test/doc-sync.sh PASS ("README and ROADMAP state v0.9.23 … ROADMAP names all 47 merged tasklists") — which also required a ROADMAP row for 901, merged at 61fc39b with none, i.e. doc-sync was already red on main. Linux NOT OBSERVED again this iteration (no docker/Linux host here); the test prints the per-key answer, so CI will record that reading now that the file is in all three gate lists.

FULL GATE, after the commit: `chief verify` -> "verify: OK (allowing merge)" and ">> chief verify: exit 0 RECORDED for tree a8dcd8e7c33137deb2795ee6613f895d9e04edf6", with the behavioural block reporting "BYSTANDER PASS — a run belonging to another install survived the behavioural block (65 test(s)) and a real sweep; a genuine orphan in a readable registry was still reaped; no fixture leaked". Note WHICH hook that was: during an agent turn the driver exports CHIEF_VERIFY_HOOK=<project checkout>/.chief/verify.sh, so the hook executed is the BASE's (65 tests) and not this branch's (66, with reap-escaped added) — the branch's list is what runs at merge, when the branch is checked out in the project. So the new file was run under the guard EXPLICITLY instead: `CHIEF_BYSTANDER_TESTS="reap-escaped" bash test/bystander.sh` -> "BYSTANDER PASS … (1 test(s))", with "one sweep, both directions: orphan 50705 reaped, bystander 49597 left alone". That matters for this test specifically — it is the one test in the suite that reaps processes on a key that did not exist before, and hermetic-in-state is not hermetic-in-processes.

userStories.title: The platform gap is stated where the next reader looks
acceptanceCriteria: `engine/reap.sh`'s key-3 note replaces 'UNVERIFIED' and 'belt-and-braces, not a proven hole' with the 2026-09-11 field record, and names the key that now covers the shape on macOS.
`chief reap -n`'s 'this key was inactive' line says which key carried the sweep in its place, so an empty result on macOS is never read as 'nothing escaped'.
The doc that documents `chief reap` carries the same record.
userStories.notes:
THREE SURFACES, one record. (1) engine/reap.sh's key-3 note: "so whether they beat key 1 is UNVERIFIED. This key is therefore belt-and-braces, not a proven hole" is GONE (grep for either phrase in engine/ and docs/ now returns nothing) and is replaced by the 2026-09-11 macOS 26.5 field record — four runs cut off around 00:58 with every driver pid dead and every state file still reading `running`, and `UnrealEditor-Cmd -unattended` on a temp engine-version-probe-<uuid>.uproject from a downstream tasklist's run: PPID 1, cwd in /Users/Shared/Epic Games/UE_5.8/…, NO argv marker, 78 minutes old, 199% CPU, ignoring SIGTERM. The note now says the hole is PROVEN, that under SIP key 3 degrades to NOTHING and cwd + argv do not cover this shape, and that what covers it is KEY 4 (engine/ledger.sh), which reads no environment at all. It also says coverage is RECORDED rather than inferred (test/reap-escaped.sh asks all four keys one at a time and prints each answer) and keeps test/teardown.sh part 4 as key 3's own pin on hosts that have it.

(2) The `chief reap -n` line, OBSERVED on this host (macOS 26.5, key 3 inert): "chief reap: no orphaned chief processes of any kind …" is now followed by "(this platform will not show another process's environment, so the inherited-$CHIEF_RUN_ID key was inactive — cwd + argv + the descendant ledger, key 4, recorded by each live run, carried this sweep)". It used to end "cwd + argv carried this sweep", which on the one host where it prints is exactly the misreading the story is about: the field escape wore NEITHER cwd nor argv. Second branch, for a host with no `ps -o lstart=` either: "…AND reports no process start times, so the inherited-$CHIEF_RUN_ID key AND the descendant-ledger key were BOTH inactive — only cwd + argv carried this sweep, and a descendant that left its worktree with a boring argv would not have been found by any key". So an empty sweep never reads as "nothing escaped" in either case. The line is asserted in flight by test/reap-escaped.sh, whose own tail prints it verbatim.

(3) docs/explanation/drivers-and-safety.md (the doc that documents `chief reap`): "Two durable markers replace it" -> FOUR durable keys, a union never a replacement, with the inherited marker and the descendant ledger written out as list entries; the sample report's key legend gained `[ledger] recorded in its run's tree while that run was live`, matching what chief_report_orphans actually prints; a new section "The key that is a record, not a search" carries the field record, why a PPID walk cannot reach a launchd-reparented process, a sample [ledger] finding, the PID-REUSED · LEFT ALONE refusal through the single chief_ledger_starttime reader, the POLL_SECONDS bound, the inactive-vs-unchecked distinction, and the empty-sweep line above. The foreign-registry rule gained one sentence: the ledger key needs no account-for-the-run rule because it only ever reads ledgers in THIS registry. ROADMAP's historical row for `77` no longer asserts "(belt-and-braces)" as a present-tense claim — it now reads "then thought belt-and-braces; proven a real hole, and covered by a fourth key, in 122".

GATES, all observed this iteration on macOS 26.5 (Darwin 25.5.0): bash -n CLEAN over bin/chief + engine/*.sh + install.sh + templates/*.sh + test/*.sh (no failures printed). shellcheck -S error CLEAN repo-wide, EXIT=0 (0.10.0, /tmp/shellcheck-v0.10.0 — brew still fails on /opt/homebrew permissions). Behavioural core: test/smoke.sh PASS (12.7s), test/ratelimit.sh PASS, test/noworkguard.sh PASS. Because this edits reap.sh: test/reap-escaped.sh REAPESC PASS (env read: none, ledger: lstart — the escapee reaped, the reused pid reported and left alone), test/reapscope.sh PASS, test/reapenv.sh PASS (with its documented end-to-end SKIP on this platform), test/teardown.sh PASS. scripts/check-doc-links.mjs: 0 dead references, 0 distinct targets. VERSION 0.9.23 -> 0.9.24 with README's and ROADMAP's bold stamps moved together; test/doc-sync.sh PASS — "README and ROADMAP state v0.9.24; README documents every bin/chief subcommand; ROADMAP names all 47 merged tasklists". quality ratchet vs main: OK — no tracked metric regressed (function_length_max 613 -> 613 tol 15, single_use_functions 61 -> 63 delta +2 tol 2 — unchanged from US-2, this story adds no helper).
